n: Chapters 25–32 turn to oracles against foreign nations. Placed between Jerusalem’s siege (ch. 24) and news of its fall (ch. 33), they show that God judges all nations, not only Israel.

f.w: The word of the LORD came again unto me

n: First, Ammon, east of the Jordan—descendants of Lot.

f.g: Descendants of Lot, living east of the Jordan around Rabbah.

n: Ammon cheered “Aha!” when the temple was profaned, the land ruined, and Judah exiled. Gloating over others’ suffering is itself a sin.
So God will give Ammon to desert tribes from the east, who will camp there and eat its produce.

f.g: Nomadic tribes from the Arabian desert.

n: Rabbah, Ammon’s capital, will become a pasture for camels and sheep.
Ammon clapped and stamped with delight, full of contempt for Israel.
God will hand Ammon over to plunder and wipe it out as a nation.

f.w: I will cause thee to perish out of the countries

n: Next Moab and Seir (Edom) said Judah was just like every other nation—denying that Israel’s God and covenant were special.

f.g: Descendants of Lot, east of the Dead Sea.
Mocking Israel’s claim to be God’s chosen people.

n: God will expose Moab’s flank by opening its border towns—its glory—to invaders.
Moab, like Ammon, will be given to the eastern tribes, and Ammon will be forgotten.

f.w: that the Ammonites may not be remembered

n: God will judge Moab, and it will know he is the Lord.

f.w: I will execute judgments upon Moab

n: Edom—Esau’s descendants—took revenge on Judah when it fell, an act that Obadiah and the Psalms remember bitterly.

f.g: Descendants of Esau, south of the Dead Sea.

n: God will lay Edom waste from Teman in the north to Dedan in the south.

f.g: An Arabian oasis southeast of Edom.

n: Strikingly, God will use Israel itself as his instrument against Edom. Later, the Hasmonean Jewish rulers did conquer the Edomites (Idumeans).

f.w: by the hand of my people Israel

n: The Philistines, Israel’s ancient coastal enemies, acted with spiteful revenge rooted in “old hatred.”

f.g: Centuries of hostility going back to the judges and Saul.

n: God will cut off the Cherethites and the rest of the coastal peoples.

f.g: Cherethites, a group linked with the Philistines and possibly from Crete.

n: God will take great vengeance on them, and they will know he is the Lord. The nations’ hatred will not have the final word over God’s people.

f.w: they shall know that I am the LORD
